status: pre-registered; no selection result had been computed when this was written
question: Does choosing jointly among several valid CDS candidates per target reduce the worst exact DNA tract shared between library members, compared with the cheaper methods already in the package, under a matched budget?
panel_selection_rule: 9S is the original six-target panel used throughout this project. 14S and 19S are the first six targets of their length in validation/integration.corpus() order, taken before any result was computed. Recorded verbatim so the choice cannot be revised after seeing outcomes.

candidates.note: Four to start. Expansion to eight happens only if four shows value, and gets its own finite budget.

shared_settings.compartment_note: A labelled benchmark fixture for continuity, not a decision about the intended expression system. The wet lab has not settled nuclear versus chloroplast.
shared_settings.check_offtarget_note: Screening is irrelevant to a DNA-sharing objective and would add a network dependency. Reported as not assessed.

primary_objective.definition: max over all distinct member pairs of homology.longest_shared(a, b)[0], computed on the full CDS

tie_breaking: fewer pairs at or above the flag threshold
lower total count of 20-mers shared between any pair
lexicographically smallest tuple of candidate seed indices
tie_breaking_note: Declared before any result was seen. The last rule is arbitrary but deterministic, so a tie cannot be resolved by whichever answer looks better.
flag_threshold_note: homology.HR_THRESHOLD_NT, unchanged. It must not be redefined to make a result pass. A shared tract is a necessary substrate for recombination, never a prediction of it.

methods.description: design_oneshot per target at the base seed; the current default
homology.diversify_library with the corrected encoding re-roll
deterministic greedy selection over the per-target candidate banks

incumbent_rule: The best complete baseline library is retained as incumbent. The joint route must fall back to it if its choice is worse on the primary objective. Per-target improvement does not imply whole-library improvement and will not be claimed as such.
secondary_reports: pairs at or above the flag threshold
candidates requested, generated, valid and distinct

budget.kind_note: Wall, not CPU. experiment.run checks it before starting each item, so one overrunning item still finishes; the budget bounds how long new work is started, not the longest possible run.
budget.on_exhaustion: Report status 'timed out' with partial results. A timeout is never reported as completion.

decision_gate.keep_the_feature_if: it improves the primary metric on at least two of the three panels, retains the incumbent when it cannot improve, and its runtime and secondary-metric costs are reported
decision_gate.otherwise: retain the cheaper workflow and publish the negative result
decision_gate.explicitly_not_claimed: Nothing here measures recombination frequency, expression, or biological performance. The objective is a sequence measurement.
